newsitem.title: UK: London clearing house changes to go ahead - King.
newsitem.headline: London clearing house changes to go ahead - King.

text.p: The change in ownership of the London Clearing House (LCH) has received overwhelming approval from its members, and will go ahead in early 1997.

At the London Metal Exchange (LME) metals seminar on Monday, LME chief Executive David King said that proposals to alter the LCH's structure had been agreed by current clearing members accounting for over 96 percent of cleared business.
LCH officials said that by the deadline of Friday October 4, 126 members out of a total 174 had sent in their letters of approval. These represented 96.3 percent of cleared activity.

The proposals included the LCH's share capital rising to 50 million stg from the current 15 million stg. To receive backing, the LCH needed 80 companies, accounting for 75 percent of cleared activity, to proceed with the change.

The LCH clears all London futures and options business on markets such as the LME and the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE), which trades financial and agricultural products.
